description: Credit card export (Type column, debits positive) with a quoted preamble row, a Netflix monthly subscription, a refund pair, six interleaved one-off merchants, and a McDonald's habit written half the time as "MCDONALD'S" (apostrophe) and half as "MCDONALDS"/"Mcdonalds" (no apostrophe) across three months, to measure whether merchant-stem grouping survives an apostrophe.

expectedCandidates.knownGap: normalizeMerchant() splits "McDonald's" on the apostrophe into a separate 'mcdonald' stem (KNOWN_CHAINS keys on the punctuation-free 'mcdonalds'). Measured: the no-apostrophe spelling ('mcdonalds', 8 of the file's 14 occurrences) clears the habit floor on its own and IS surfaced; the apostrophe spelling ('mcdonald', the other 6) stays under the floor and is silently dropped. Net effect: the habit is found, but its occurrence count and total undercount the merchant's true frequency by 6/14 (~43%), and any punctuation variant alone (without a majority no-apostrophe group) would be missed outright.
